gates.meaning: Continuous online learning ends closer to the current resident coordinate family than its identically pretrained frozen counterpart in at least 7/8 worlds.
Online continuation preserves a richer written-operator family than freezing the same learner in at least 7/8 worlds.
Online continuation preserves stronger A→B versus B→A composition separation than the frozen learner in at least 7/8 worlds.
A continually updated imperfect learner beats an initially perfect modal basis that is left behind as the computation moves.
The continuation advantage survives the functional composition readout.
The online learner remains bounded by the current-coordinate oracle.
The online composition result remains bounded by the moving oracle.

supported: In this constructed slowly drifting recurrent family, continued online Sanger-style coordinate learning preserves the current write/operator organization better than freezing the same learner before drift.

A perfect initial modal basis becomes functionally worse than an imperfect basis that continues to adapt, supporting the narrow statement that computational identity behaves like a continuation rather than a fixed coordinate location in this world.
limited: The drift is smooth, low-dimensional and slow relative to the learner; the system is still a constructed symmetric linear recurrence.
Periodic Gram-Schmidt stabilization makes this Sanger-style learner online but not strictly synapse-local.
No delayed credit signal is transported yet; this gate tests coordinate identity/continuation, not ThirdWay's full credit-transport claim.

limitations: The hidden mode rotation law is supplied by the synthetic world.
The online learner receives raw state samples but not sparse event-limited observations.
The final operator audit uses the same synthetic write law as v2.
The next gate should add delayed credit or task learning whose eligibility trace must follow the moving coordinates.
